guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our disagreement with the market starts with South Florida’s offensive balance. Our numbers rate the passing and rushing attacks among the nation’s most efficient, and Temple has struggled to prevent scoring opportunities. That combination gives South Florida multiple ways to sustain drives and create separation rather than relying on one specific matchup.

The concern for us is Temple’s ability to respond on the ground. Temple rushed for 697 yards through three games, clearing 186 yards each time, and converted every red-zone opportunity over that span. That production could shorten the game and keep the margin competitive. We still lean more strongly toward South Florida than the market does, but the available price does not create enough value for us to get involved.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching South Florida’s passing offense against Temple’s pass defense. Temple allowed 297.3 passing yards per game through three games, while opponents converted 51.3 percent of their third downs. Against a South Florida passing attack ranked fourth in pass EPA, those extended drives could turn into the scoring opportunities our model expects.

The question is whether Temple can get off the field often enough to control the margin. If it cannot, South Florida’s offensive versatility supports our model’s stronger view of the home team.

recent_game.fact: Temple lost 49-48 in overtime at Toledo, falling to 1-2.
Temple led Toledo 24-14 at halftime and 42-28 with 6:40 remaining, but Toledo scored twice in the final 1:05 and tied the game with 54 seconds left.
Ajani Sheppard threw touchdown passes to Joey Schlaffer, Sam Brown and Colin Chase against Toledo; the 69-yard score to Chase gave Temple a 35-28 fourth-quarter lead.
Sheppard scored on a 22-yard run in overtime, but Temple's ensuing two-point pass attempt failed.
In his first game action for Temple, Sam Brown rushed for a career-high 109 yards and scored three combined touchdowns against Toledo.
Kevin Hornbeak forced a fumble on Toledo's first offensive play and Saboor Karriem recovered it.

quarterback.fact: Temple's quarterback room is led by transfers Jaxon Smolik, formerly of Penn State, and Ajani Sheppard, formerly of Washington State and Rutgers.
The participation streak table lists Smolik with starts in each of Temple's first three games and Sheppard with appearances in all three games but no starts.
Sheppard's two-yard fourth-down touchdown pass to Joey Schlaffer against Toledo was the first touchdown pass of Sheppard's career.

offensive_personnel.fact: Temple returned four 2025 offensive-line starters: left tackle Giakoby Hills, left guard Eric King, center Grayson Mains and right guard Jackson Pruitt.
Rutgers transfer Zach Aamland entered the starting lineup because of injuries in Week 1 and is described as one of Temple's starting tackles.
The current-streak table lists John Stone with three starts, Zach Aamland and freshman John Watkins with two starts apiece, and Kevin Terry with one appearance through three games.
Sam Brown transferred to Temple for his fifth season after spending four seasons at Rutgers.
Penn State transfer Joey Schlaffer joined Temple's tight end room and caught a touchdown against Toledo.
Peter Clarke recorded 30 receptions and six touchdown catches in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: Linebacker Curly Ordonez led Temple in tackles in each of the first three games of 2026 after leading the team in tackles in 2025.
Safety Saboor Karriem, a transfer from Illinois, started each of Temple's first three games and recovered a fumble against Toledo.
Defensive lineman Kevin Hornbeak, outside linebacker Jaylon Joseph, linebacker Eric Stuart and safety Saboor Karriem each started Temple's first three games.
Temple added five safeties during the January transfer window: Saboor Karriem, Kolin Dinkins, Jaeden Gould, Orel Gray and Josiah Jackson.

coaching_changes.fact: Temple retained offensive coordinator Tyler Walker, defensive coordinator Brian L. Smith and special teams coordinator Brian Ginn from 2025 for their second seasons under K.C. Keeler.

injury_availability.fact: Cornerback Devontae Ward-Grant will miss the entire 2026 season after suffering an injury during the spring.
Right-tackle candidate Luke Watson worked with the first team during spring and summer before an injury gave Kevin Terry an opportunity on the right side.
